studies.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1: full painting to repair.
Image 2: diagnostic crop showing the defect, NOT a style reference.
Remove the repeated triangular/diamond-shaped swatches that form a faint tessellated pattern across the middle of the painting. They can be seen crossing the red sail, the sky near the horizon, the chimneys and gable walls. This is an unwanted image artifact, not intended brushwork or material texture.
Repaint those surfaces as continuous, softly shaded forms. The sky must have uninterrupted smooth colour gradients between cloud shapes. The sail must have clean matte red colour with only its few large physical folds. Chimneys and plaster gables must have coherent broad light and shadow following their actual geometry, without patches. Keep real roof tiles only on the roofs. Keep irregular water reflections only on the water.
Preserve the composition, framing, positions of every object, colours, light direction, low rear view, rounded wooden boat, lantern, red sail silhouette, drowned houses, trees, church and lighthouse from image 1. Preserve the complete mast. Do not redesign the scene. Do not blur the whole picture: retain clear silhouette edges and resolve the interiors cleanly. Use smoothly blended colour rather than simulated brush dabs.
No triangular mosaic, polygon facets, diagonal crosshatching, diamonds, chevrons, repeating swatches, canvas grain or added global texture. No text. Same landscape aspect ratio.
studies.assessment: Sail improved, faceting remained on chimney and gable at 200%.
